info.title: Flashduty Open API
info.description: Public HTTP API for the Flashduty incident management platform — incidents, notification templates, channels, schedules, monitors, RUM, and platform administration. Every operation is authenticated with an `app_key` query parameter created in the Flashduty console under My → APP Key (or sent in the `Fd-App-Key` header). Responses follow a uniform envelope: `{ request_id, data }` on success, `{ request_id, error }` on failure.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **300 requests/minute**; **20 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | **Datasources Manage** (`monit`) |

## Usage

- `type_ident` must be one of: `prometheus`, `loki`, `mysql`, `oracle`, `postgres`, `clickhouse`, `elasticsearch`, `sls`, `tencent_cls`, `victorialogs`, `redis_node`, `redis_sentinel`, `mongodb_mongod`, `mongodb_mongos`, `kafka`. The last five (`redis_node`, `redis_sentinel`, `mongodb_mongod`, `mongodb_mongos`, `kafka`) are diagnostic-only: they cannot evaluate alerts, so `alerting_enabled` must not be `true`.
- `name` must be unique within the account across all types; a duplicate fails with `InvalidParameter`.
- `edge_cluster_name` must be an existing Monitors edge cluster of the account; that cluster evaluates rules and runs queries for the datasource.
- Put the type-specific settings in `payload.<type_ident>`. For `elasticsearch`, `payload.elasticsearch.deployment` is required (`cloud` or `self-managed`). `tencent_cls` requires every edge instance in the cluster to run Monitors edge v0.66.0 or later.
- Omitted `enabled` defaults to `true`; omitted `alerting_enabled` defaults to `true` for alerting types and `false` for diagnostic-only types. Explicit `null` for either is rejected.
- `manage_team_id` and `readonly_team_ids` restrict who can manage or query the datasource; omit both to leave it open to every member.
- Responses return credentials of non-diagnostic types (for example Prometheus Basic Auth passwords) as stored. Diagnostic passwords and Kafka private keys are returned only when they are `${env:NAME}` references. Treat responses as sensitive.
- Every call is recorded in the account audit log.

post.description: Update a datasource by ID, replacing its name, note, address, payload and edge cluster.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **300 requests/minute**; **20 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | **Datasources Manage** (`monit`) |

## Usage

- This is a full replace, not a patch: send `type_ident`, `name`, `edge_cluster_name`, `payload` and (except for Elasticsearch `cloud`) `address` on every call. `note`, `address` and `payload` overwrite the stored values, so an omitted `note` is cleared.
- Omitting `enabled`, `alerting_enabled`, `manage_team_id` or `readonly_team_ids` keeps the current value. `null` for `enabled` or `alerting_enabled` is rejected; `null` for the two team fields clears them.
- Secrets: for the diagnostic types, omit the password (and the Kafka `tls_key`) to keep the stored value or send an empty string to clear it. For `tencent_cls`, an omitted or empty `secret_key` keeps the stored key. Other types need their credentials resent.
- Setting `enabled` or `alerting_enabled` to `false`, or changing `type_ident` or `edge_cluster_name`, closes open alerts of the rules that use this datasource. Renaming it closes open alerts of rules whose `ds_list` name pattern no longer matches the new name.
- Turning `alerting_enabled` off fails with HTTP 409 `UndonedOrderExist` while an enabled alert rule still selects the datasource.
- Only the account owner, Admin members, the creator and members of the managing team can update a datasource (anyone with the permission when no managing team is set); others get `AccessDenied`. An unknown ID, or one in another account, returns `ResourceNotFound`.
- Every call is recorded in the account audit log.

post.description: Run a synchronous ad-hoc query against a data source and return a `query_result.v1` result as frames, records, or samples.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **100 requests/minute**; **5 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | Any valid `app_key` (read-only; not gated by a specific permission class) |
| Edge requirement | Supported deployments require **monit-edge v0.65.0 or later** |

## Usage

- The data source is identified by `ds_type` plus `ds_name`, not by ID. It must belong to the account and be enabled. When the data source restricts querying to certain teams, only members of those teams, its managing team, and account owners or admins can query it; others get `AccessDenied`.
- Treat **monit-edge v0.65.0** as the minimum supported Edge version for this public API. WebAPI retains migration adapters for older Edge versions: query.v2 results may still preserve frames, records, or samples, while legacy rows can expose only the information they retained. These adapters do not change the support floor; older protocols lack query.v3 cancellation and error-lifecycle semantics, and data already lost by legacy rows cannot be recovered.
- The public response format is always `query_result.v1` and is independent of the internal Edge query protocol. Dispatch on `result.kind` (`frames`, `records`, or `samples`); do not infer the result shape from `ds_type` or the Edge version.
- A `frames` result may contain multiple table or time-series frames. Field values are columnar and all fields in one frame have the same length.
- A `records` result may contain nested JSON and null records. Integer literals outside JavaScript's safe integer range are returned as decimal strings.
- A `samples` result contains label sets and instant values. A value may be a number or one of the strings `NaN`, `+Inf`, and `-Inf`.
- Prometheus expressions are syntax-checked before the query is dispatched; an invalid expression returns HTTP 400.
- The request body is limited to 256 KiB and the complete success response to 10 MiB; either limit returns HTTP 413. A result with more than 1,000 rows fails with HTTP 400. Narrow the time range, reduce fields, or aggregate at the source.
- Query failures use non-2xx HTTP status codes and the standard error envelope.
- Query execution may take up to 35 seconds across WebAPI forwarding and Edge execution. Configure client timeouts to at least 40 seconds and propagate cancellation when the caller abandons a query.

## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **2,000 requests/minute**; **32 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | **Datasources Read** (`monit`) |

Use datasource IDs from `/monit/datasource/list`. Disabled datasources return `datasource_disabled`; `alerting_enabled=false` does not block tools. Errors use non-2xx HTTP status and `error.code`, `error.message`, `error.reason`. `tool_not_supported` indicates the selected executor does not provide this tool; it is not a vendor permission error. Never retry through another Edge or the legacy diagnose endpoint automatically.

## Usage

- The caller needs query access to the datasource (see `readonly_team_ids` on the datasource); without it the call fails with 403 `access_denied`. A datasource in another account returns 404 `datasource_not_found`.
- Diagnostic tools exist only for datasource types `mysql`, `postgres`, `redis_node`, `redis_sentinel`, `mongodb_mongod`, `mongodb_mongos`, `kafka`, `elasticsearch`, `prometheus`, `loki` and `victorialogs`; `oracle`, `clickhouse`, `sls` and `tencent_cls` support only their `<type>.query` tool. Other combinations fail with `invalid_request`.
- Two tool families share this entry: diagnostic tools defined by the executing Edge (e.g. `mysql.overview`, `prometheus.metric_trends`) and query tools named `<type>.query`. The tool prefix must match the datasource type.
- Query tools require the Edge cluster to support Explore queries (protocol milestone v0.68.0); diagnostic tools require the v0.71.0 base invoke protocol. Unsupported clusters fail with `edge_upgrade_required`, `mixed_edge_versions`, or `edge_version_unknown`; never fall back to `/monit/query/data` or another endpoint automatically.
- For query tools, `params` follows the per-datasource schema named in the `tool` field description. `expr` and `execution` are always required. `limit`/`direction` only bound raw-log retrieval, never SQL rows or scanned data. Unknown extension fields are tolerated but never executed or forwarded.
- Query `data` is the complete Explore result: `format` is `explore_result.v1` and `result.kind` is `samples`, `frames`, or `logs`; log results keep `applied_limit` and `has_more`. Query results never synthesize `summary` or `truncated`.
- Request body limit 128 KiB; complete success response limit 10 MiB for both families; diagnostic tool timeout at most 25 seconds.

400.description: Standard HTTP error. `error.reason` is `invalid_request` for malformed or out-of-range parameters, a disabled data source, an unsupported data source type, or a data source without an Edge cluster. A data source ID that does not exist returns code `ResourceNotFound` without a `reason`.

403.description: The caller is not allowed to query this data source. `error.code` is `AccessDenied`; there is no `error.reason`.

413.description: Standard HTTP error. `error.reason`: `too_many_rows`, `source_too_large`, or `result_too_large`. A request body above 256 KiB also returns 413, without a `reason`.

type_ident.description:
Datasource type.

Alerting types (can evaluate alert rules):
- `prometheus`: Prometheus-compatible metrics.
- `loki`: Grafana Loki logs.
- `mysql`: MySQL.
- `oracle`: Oracle Database.
- `postgres`: PostgreSQL.

- `elasticsearch`: Elasticsearch.
- `sls`: Alibaba Cloud Simple Log Service.
- `tencent_cls`: Tencent Cloud Log Service (CLS).
- `victorialogs`: VictoriaLogs.

Diagnostic-only types (cannot evaluate alerts, `alerting_enabled` is always `false`):
- `redis_node`: a single Redis node.
- `redis_sentinel`: Redis Sentinel.
- `mongodb_mongod`: a MongoDB mongod instance.
- `mongodb_mongos`: a MongoDB mongos router.
- `kafka`: a Kafka cluster.

The `payload` key that holds the type-specific settings has the same name as the type.

name.description: Datasource name, unique within the account across all types.

enabled.description: Whether business execution is enabled. Disabled datasources reject business queries and tools; enabling does not change alerting_enabled.

note.description: Free-text note; an empty string when not set.

address.description: Connection address as stored, after normalization. The format depends on `type_ident`; see the `address` field of the create request for each type. At most 4096 characters.

payload.description: Type-specific configuration block; must contain the key matching `type_ident`. Always `null` in `/monit/datasource/list` responses (the list query does not read the payload column); populated in create/update/info responses. For `tencent_cls`, `secret_key` is masked to an empty string unless it is an `${env:...}` reference. For diagnostic types, password and Kafka tls_key are omitted from responses unless they are ${env:...} references. On update, omit those fields to preserve stored secrets; explicitly send an empty string to clear. Other configuration fields retain their existing behavior.

edge_cluster_name.description: Monitors edge cluster name responsible for evaluating rules using this datasource.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp, Unix epoch seconds.

alerting_enabled.description: Whether alert evaluation is allowed. Alerting also requires enabled=true and an alerting-capable type. Always false for diagnostic-only types; false does not block non-alerting queries or tools.

manage_team_id.description: ID of the managing team. Its members can edit, delete, enable or disable the datasource and view its full configuration. `null` means no managing team: any caller with the Datasources Manage permission can manage it. The creator, the account owner and Admin members can always manage.

readonly_team_ids.description: IDs of the teams allowed to query and reference the datasource, in addition to the managing team, the creator, the account owner and Admin members. `null` or an empty array means every member of the account can query it.

creator_id.description: ID of the member who created the datasource; `null` when not recorded. The creator can always manage the datasource.

The caller's access level on this datasource. Only present in list responses.
- `manage`: can edit, delete, enable or disable the datasource, view its configuration and query it.
- `readonly`: can query and reference the datasource but not change it or read its configuration.

Datasource type.

Alerting types (can evaluate alert rules):
- `prometheus`: Prometheus-compatible metrics.
- `loki`: Grafana Loki logs.
- `mysql`: MySQL.

- `postgres`: PostgreSQL.

Diagnostic-only types (cannot evaluate alerts, `alerting_enabled` is always `false`):
- `redis_node`: a single Redis node.
- `redis_sentinel`: Redis Sentinel.
- `mongodb_mongod`: a MongoDB mongod instance.
- `mongodb_mongos`: a MongoDB mongos router.
- `kafka`: a Kafka cluster.

The `payload` key that holds the type-specific settings has the same name as the type.

name.description: Datasource name; required and unique within the account across all types. This is the name referenced as `ds_name` in query APIs. Duplicates fail with `InvalidParameter`.

note.description: Free-text note. On update, an omitted or empty value clears the stored note.

address.description:
Connection address, required for every type except `elasticsearch` with `deployment: cloud`. At most 4096 characters after normalization. Format by type:
- `prometheus`, `loki`, `victorialogs`: HTTP URL; `http://` is prepended when the value does not start with `http`.
- `mysql`, `oracle`, `postgres`: `host:port`.
- `clickhouse`: one or more comma-separated `host:port` endpoints; duplicates are rejected.
- `elasticsearch` with `self-managed`: one or more comma-separated HTTP(S) URLs (scheme defaults to `http://`) that share identical query parameters; duplicates are rejected. Not needed for `cloud`.
- `sls`: endpoint without the `http://` or `https://` prefix.
- `tencent_cls`: exactly `cls.tencentcloudapi.com` or `cls.internal.tencentcloudapi.com` (requires Monitors edge >= v0.66.0).
- `redis_node`, `redis_sentinel`, `mongodb_mongod`, `mongodb_mongos`: a single `host:port` (bracket IPv6) with no URI, userinfo or query.
- `kafka`: 1-32 unique comma-separated `host:port` bootstrap addresses (the payload has no broker list).

payload.description: Type-specific configuration block; must include the key named by `type_ident`. An update replaces the whole payload, so resend every setting you want to keep (including credentials of non-diagnostic types, which the info endpoint returns). Exceptions: for the diagnostic types, omit the password (and the Kafka `tls_key`) to keep the stored value or send an empty string to clear it; for `tencent_cls`, an omitted or empty `secret_key` keeps the stored key. Stored secrets are not carried over when `type_ident` changes.

edge_cluster_name.description: Name of the Monitors edge cluster that evaluates rules and runs queries for this datasource. It must be an existing edge cluster of the account, otherwise the call fails with `InvalidParameter`. Changing it on update closes open alerts of rules that use this datasource.

enabled.description: Whether business execution is enabled. Omitted on create: true; omitted on update: preserve the current value. Explicit false disables execution; null is invalid. Does not change alerting_enabled.

alerting_enabled.description: Whether this datasource may evaluate alerts. Omitted on create: true for alerting types, false for diagnostic-only types; omitted on update: preserve current value. null is invalid. redis_node, redis_sentinel, mongodb_mongod, mongodb_mongos and kafka reject true. Disabling is rejected with conflict when enabled rules reference the datasource.

manage_team_id.description: ID of the managing team (see the response field of the same name). On create, omitted means no managing team. On update, omitted keeps the current value, while `null` or `0` clears it. Required whenever `readonly_team_ids` is non-empty.

readonly_team_ids.description: IDs of the teams allowed to query and reference the datasource (see the response field of the same name). On create, omitted means unrestricted. On update, omitted keeps the current value, while `null` or an empty array clears it (everyone can query). Duplicates and `0` are dropped. Requires `manage_team_id`: a non-empty list without a managing team fails with `InvalidParameter`.

ds_type.description:
Data source type. Together with `ds_name` it must match an enabled data source of the account.

- `prometheus`: Prometheus-compatible data source; `expr` is PromQL.
- `loki`: Grafana Loki; `expr` is LogQL.
- `victorialogs`: VictoriaLogs.
- `sls`: Alibaba Cloud Log Service (SLS).
- `tencent_cls`: Tencent Cloud Log Service (CLS); requires monit-edge v0.66.0 or later.
- `elasticsearch`: Elasticsearch.
- `mysql`: MySQL; `expr` is SQL.
- `postgres`: PostgreSQL; `expr` is SQL.
- `oracle`: Oracle Database; `expr` is SQL.
- `clickhouse`: ClickHouse; `expr` is SQL.

Other data source types (for example MongoDB, Redis, or Kafka) are rejected.

expr.description: Query expression in the language of `ds_type` (PromQL for `prometheus`, LogQL for `loki`, SQL for SQL sources, and so on). Required, at most 64 KiB (12 KiB for `tencent_cls`). Loki's `$__auto` is not supported here; use a fixed duration such as `[5m]`. Prometheus expressions are syntax-checked before dispatch.

delay_seconds.description: Look-back offset in seconds, from 0 to 86400. Applied to point-in-time queries (Prometheus, Loki stats, VictoriaLogs stats); ignored for raw and detail queries. When `args` carries an absolute `<source>.time` and the Edge is v0.74.0 or later, the absolute time takes precedence and this offset is not applied.

args.description:
Extra query parameters as string key/value pairs; keys are namespaced by data source (for example `sls.project`, `loki.type`). At most 128 entries, keys up to 256 bytes, values up to 64 KiB, and 128 KiB in total. What is accepted depends on `ds_type`:

- `prometheus`: optional `prometheus.time`, the evaluation time as Unix seconds, not in the future.
- `loki`, `victorialogs`: `<source>.type` is `stats` (default) or `raw`. `stats` accepts an optional `<source>.time` (Unix seconds, not in the future). `raw` requires a time range, either `<source>.start` + `<source>.end` (Unix seconds) or `<source>.timespan.value` + `<source>.timespan.unit` (`s`, `m`, `h`, or `d`), spanning at most 6 hours, and accepts `<source>.limit` from 1 to 1001.
- `sls`: `sls.project` and `sls.logstore` are required. Optional: `sls.lines` (1 to 100), `sls.offset` (0 or more), and a time range of at most 6 hours given as `sls.from` + `sls.to` (Unix seconds) or `sls.timespan.value` + `sls.timespan.unit`.
- `tencent_cls`: `tencent_cls.region`, `tencent_cls.topic_id`, `tencent_cls.query_mode` (`raw` or `analysis`), and `tencent_cls.syntax` (`cql` or `lucene`) are required. Optional: `tencent_cls.limit` (1 to 100, `raw` mode only, needs monit-edge v0.67.0 or later) and a time range given as `tencent_cls.from` + `tencent_cls.to` (Unix seconds) or `tencent_cls.timespan.value` + `tencent_cls.timespan.unit`, at most 6 hours in `raw` mode and 24 hours in `analysis` mode. Any other key is rejected.
- `elasticsearch`: `es.type` may be `sql` or omitted; any other value is rejected.
- `mysql`, `postgres`, `oracle`, `clickhouse`: no arguments are defined.

An absolute `<source>.time` is only valid for its own data source type. Edges older than v0.74.0 approximate it with a look-back offset and accept only times within the last 86,400 seconds.

VictoriaLogsQueryParams.description: victorialogs.query parameters. `expr` is LogsQL. Use `window` for raw logs (`limit`/`direction` allowed) or `instant`/`range` with `from_ms` for stats queries (`limit`/`direction` rejected).

expr.description: Query expression evaluated by the datasource; dialect depends on the datasource type.

limit.description: Maximum raw-log entries to return (1–100). Only bounds raw logs, not SQL rows or scanned data; omitted keeps the executor default. Explicit null is invalid.

direction.description: Raw-log retrieval order: `latest` returns the newest entries first, `earliest` the oldest. Omitted keeps the executor default.

powersql.description: Whether to run the query with SLS PowerSQL. Omitted keeps the executor default; explicit null is invalid.

SLSQueryParams.description: sls.query parameters for Alibaba Cloud SLS. `execution.kind` must be `window`.

expr.description: Query expression evaluated by the datasource; dialect depends on the datasource type.

limit.description: Maximum raw-log entries to return (1–1000). Only bounds raw logs, not SQL rows or scanned data; omitted keeps the executor default. Explicit null is invalid.

direction.description: Raw-log retrieval order: `latest` returns the newest entries first, `earliest` the oldest. Omitted keeps the executor default.

TencentCLSQueryParams.description: tencent_cls.query parameters for Tencent Cloud CLS. `execution.kind` must be `window`.

account_id.description: Optional consistency check; must equal the authenticated account.

datasource_id.description: ID of the datasource to run the tool against, from `/monit/datasource/list`. The caller needs query access to it. For query tools (`<type>.query`) the ID must not exceed 9007199254740991.

params.description: Tool-specific JSON parameters; omitted means {}. Explicit null is invalid. Query tools (`<type>.query`) use the per-datasource params schemas named in the `tool` description.

tool.description: Single tool name prefixed by the datasource type. Diagnostic tools are defined by the executing Edge (e.g. `mysql.overview`). Query tools are `<type>.query` where `<type>` is one of `prometheus`, `mysql`, `postgres`, `oracle`, `clickhouse`, `elasticsearch`, `loki`, `victorialogs`, `sls`, `tencent_cls`; their `params` follow `PrometheusQueryParams`, `MySQLQueryParams`, `PostgresQueryParams`, `OracleQueryParams`, `ClickHouseQueryParams`, `ElasticsearchQueryParams`, `LokiQueryParams`, `VictoriaLogsQueryParams`, `SLSQueryParams`, or `TencentCLSQueryParams` respectively.

data.description: Tool-specific JSON evidence, preserved without conversion; never null. No nested legacy diagnose envelope.

tool.description: Executed tool name matching the request.

reason.description: Why the result was truncated, as reported by the executing Edge; treat it as an opaque string. The object is present only when the result was truncated.

QueryExploreRequest.description: Explore query request. All four top-level fields are required and unknown fields are rejected.

datasource_id.description: Data source ID from `/monit/datasource/list`. Must be a positive JavaScript-safe integer for an enabled data source of the authenticated account that the caller may query.

expr.description: Query expression in the data source's native language (PromQL, LogsQL, SQL, and so on). Non-empty UTF-8 of at most 64 KiB; `mysql` allows at most 16 KiB and `tencent_cls` at most 12 KiB.

args.description: Macro substitutions keyed by variable name, used for Grafana-style variables. Keys are at most 256 bytes, values at most 64 KiB, with a 128 KiB total budget.

QueryExploreExecution.description: Time semantics of the query. The accepted companion fields depend on `kind`: `instant` takes `to_ms` (and optionally `from_ms`), `range` requires `from_ms`, `to_ms`, and `max_data_points`, and `window` takes only `from_ms` and `to_ms`. When both times are present, `from_ms` must be less than `to_ms`. `step_seconds` is never accepted over HTTP.

kind.description:
Execution kind.

- `instant`: evaluate at a single point in time.
- `range`: evaluate a series over `from_ms` to `to_ms`, with a step derived from `max_data_points` and `min_step_seconds`.
- `window`: query the interval from `from_ms` to `to_ms` with no step.

from_ms.description: Start of the interval as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds; non-negative and less than `to_ms`. Required for `range` and `window`; optional for `instant`.

to_ms.description: End of the interval (or the evaluation time for `instant`) as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds; non-negative. Required for every execution kind.

max_data_points.description: Maximum number of points to return. Required for `range` and rejected for `instant` and `window`.

min_step_seconds.description: Lower bound, in seconds, for the step derived from `max_data_points`. Optional and only accepted for `range`.

ExploreResult.description: Result body. Exactly one of `frames`, `samples`, or `entries` is present and matches `kind`.

kind.description: Result shape. `frames` returns columnar tables or time series, `samples` returns instant values with labels, and `logs` returns log entries.

frames.description: Columnar frames. Present when `kind` is `frames`; at most 1,000 frames, 1,000 table rows in total, and 100,000 values in total.

samples.description: Instant samples. Present when `kind` is `samples`; at most 1,000 samples.

entries.description: Log entries. Present when `kind` is `logs`; never longer than `applied_limit`.

applied_limit.description: Entry limit applied to a logs result: 1 to 1000 (1 to 100 for `sls` data sources). Present only when `kind` is `logs`.

has_more.description: Whether a logs result was truncated by `applied_limit`.

ExploreFrame.description: One columnar frame. Every field in the frame has the same number of values.

kind.description: Frame shape. `table` is an unlabeled table. `time_series` carries exactly one time field and one float field; its time values are strictly increasing and never null.

ExploreField.description: One column of a frame. Values are columnar and may contain nulls.

name.description: Column name, at most 1 MiB of UTF-8.

type.description: Column type. `string` is rejected inside a `time_series` frame; `float` holds numbers and `time` holds UTC RFC3339Nano strings.

labels.description: Label set of this column. Only `time_series` value fields may carry labels; a `table` field must not.

items.description: One cell. `time` cells are UTC RFC3339Nano strings; `float` cells may be the strings `NaN`, `+Inf`, and `-Inf`; any cell may be null except a time value inside a `time_series` frame.

labels.description: Label set of the sample. May be empty but never null.

value.description: Sample value: a number, or one of the strings `NaN`, `+Inf`, and `-Inf`. Never null.

timestamp_ns.description: Entry time as a canonical unsigned decimal string of Unix epoch nanoseconds, at most 20 digits.

fields.description: Log fields as raw JSON values. Integer literals outside JavaScript's safe integer range are returned as decimal strings.

ExploreResponseExecution.description: Execution actually used, present when the data source returned a stepped result.

kind.description: Execution kind; always `range` when this object is present.

effective_step_seconds.description: Step, in seconds, the query was executed with after applying `max_data_points` and `min_step_seconds`.

PrometheusLabelValuesResponse.description: Native Prometheus HTTP API response returned by the queried data source. This endpoint does not wrap the payload in the Flashduty response envelope.

status.description: Prometheus result status. `success` carries `data`; `error` carries `errorType` and `error`.

errorType.description: Prometheus error class, present when `status` is `error`.

error.description: Human-readable Prometheus error message, present when `status` is `error`.

AlertRuleV2.description: Complete V2 alert rule configuration. The core difference from V1 lives in `rule_configs`: the three checkers describe recovery and ending semantics with the lifecycle v2 `recovery_mode`/`end_mode` enums.

id.description: Rule ID. Required on update; omit on create (assigned by the server).

account_id.description: Account ID, filled by the server from the authentication context; any client-supplied value is ignored.

folder_id.description: ID of the folder the rule belongs to; list folders via `POST /monit/folder/list`. Cannot be changed through the update API — use `/monit/rule/move` instead.

name.description: Rule name. Must be unique within the folder and at most 128 characters.

labels.description: Custom labels added to every alert event of the rule. Keys are trimmed, must not be empty and must not start with `__alert_rule_` (reserved); values containing `{{` are rendered as templates when events are delivered; `job` and `instance` values are limited to 255 characters. The serialized object may not exceed 1024 characters.

ds_type.description: Datasource type the rule queries. When the rule is enabled it must be a type that supports alerting: `prometheus`, `elasticsearch`, `loki`, `clickhouse`, `mysql`, `oracle`, `postgres`, `sls`, `tencent_cls`, `victorialogs`.

ds_list.description: Datasource name match patterns (wildcards supported). At least one of `ds_list` / `ds_ids` must be non-empty; both are merged to decide which datasources the rule monitors.

ds_ids.description: Datasource ID list, merged with `ds_list` to decide the monitored datasources; IDs survive datasource renames. At least one of `ds_list` / `ds_ids` must be provided.

enabled.description: Whether the rule is enabled. Required — the server enforces an explicit value (including `false`) while decoding. Setting it to `false` on update clears the rule's active alerts.

debug_log_enabled.description: Enable debug logging; the edge then emits detailed evaluation logs for this rule, useful when the rule does not trigger as expected.

rule_configs.description: Detection configuration: query list plus trigger/recovery conditions. See `AlertRuleConfigsV2`.

cron_pattern.description: Schedule expression: a 6-field cron with seconds (e.g. `0 * * * * *`), a descriptor such as `@hourly`, or `@every <duration>` with a whole number of seconds of at least `1s` (e.g. `@every 30s`). Must not start with `CRON_TZ=` or `TZ=`; set the timezone in the `timezone` field instead.

timezone.description: Timezone the rule runs in; it decides how the cron schedule and enabled time windows are interpreted. Only IANA names are accepted (e.g. `Asia/Shanghai`, `UTC`, `Europe/London`); abbreviations or offsets like `Local`, `UTC+8`, `CST` are rejected. Empty falls back to `Asia/Shanghai`.

delay_seconds.description: Seconds the evaluation query window is shifted back, compensating for data ingestion latency.

enabled_times.description: Time windows during which the rule is in effect. When omitted or empty, the rule is active 00:00–23:59 every day.

days.description: Days of week the window applies to, `0` = Sunday through `6` = Saturday; non-empty, no duplicates.

annotations.description: Extra annotation key-value pairs delivered with alert events; keys must not start with `$` (reserved for query fields).

description_type.description: Format of the description content. Empty or omitted defaults to `text`. `text` = plain text; `markdown` = Markdown, rendered as such in alert details.

description.description: Rule description; rendered as plain text or Markdown according to `description_type`.

channel_ids.description: Collaboration space IDs alerts are sent to. May be empty; alerts then route through the global integration.

repeat_interval.description: Notification repeat interval in seconds. Values below 1 fall back to the default 3600; maximum 2147483647.

repeat_total.description: Maximum number of repeat notifications. Values below 1 fall back to the default 3; maximum 2147483647.

investigation_targets.description: Drill-down entries linked from the alert event detail page; at most 20 items, duplicates rejected, and at most 32 KiB once serialized. On update the field is presence-based: omit it to keep the current value, pass `[]` to clear; `null` is rejected.

creator_id.description: Creator member ID, filled by the server from the current user; any client-supplied value is ignored.

creator_name.description: Creator name, filled by the server; any client-supplied value is ignored.

updater_id.description: ID of the member who last updated the rule, filled by the server; any client-supplied value is ignored.

updater_name.description: Name of the member who last updated the rule, filled by the server; any client-supplied value is ignored.

created_at.description: Creation time as a Unix timestamp in seconds, generated by the server; any client-supplied value is ignored.

updated_at.description: Last update time as a Unix timestamp in seconds, generated by the server; any client-supplied value is ignored.

queries.description: Query list with at least one entry; each needs a unique `name` (`R` and `__all__` are reserved) and a non-empty, non-duplicated `expr`.

name.description: Query identifier (e.g. `A`), must match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*`; `R` and `__all__` are reserved and cannot be used.

expr.description: Query expression.

label_fields.description: Result fields used as alert event labels; rows with the same label set form one alert. Must not overlap `value_fields`; applies to tabular results (SQL/ES-like datasources).

value_fields.description: Numeric result fields evaluated by threshold expressions (referenced as `$A.<field>`); required for threshold checks when the datasource is not `prometheus`/`loki`/`victorialogs`. Field names must not contain `.`.

args.description: Datasource-specific query parameters; keys follow the `<datasource>.<param>` convention (e.g. `es.type`, `tencent_cls.limit`). Most datasources need none.

relate_queries.description: Optional auxiliary queries whose results attach to alert events as context. Each entry needs a unique `name` (not colliding with any query name) and a non-empty `expr`. Always returned, as `[]` when there are none.

name.description: Auxiliary query identifier.

expr.description: Query expression.

args.description: Datasource-specific parameters for the auxiliary query; same convention as `queries[].args`.

check_anydata.description: Any-data check configuration: fires when a query returns any data row. See `AlertRuleAnyDataV2`.

enabled.description: Whether the threshold check is enabled.

alerting_check_times.description: Fire after the alert condition is met this many times; when enabled, minimum 1 and maximum 10000. Combined with `alerting_window_size` it means at least N hits within the last M evaluations.

alerting_window_size.description: Optional sliding window size M: fire only when the condition is met at least `alerting_check_times` times within the last M evaluations. Omit for consecutive mode (N consecutive hits). Must satisfy `alerting_check_times` <= M <= 10000.

recovery_check_times.description: Recover after the recovery condition is met this many times; minimum 1 when enabled.

critical.description: Critical threshold expression referencing query results as `$<query>` or `$<query>.<value_field>`, e.g. `$A > 90`; when enabled at least one of the three severities must be set.

warning.description: Warning threshold expression; same syntax as `critical`.

info.description: Info threshold expression; same syntax as `critical`.

recovery_mode.description: How recovery is decided (lifecycle v2); required when enabled. `condition_clear` = recover once the alert expression no longer holds; `recovery` is not allowed. `expression_match` = recover when the `recovery.expr` threshold expression holds. `recovery_query_match` = recover when the `recovery.expr` query expression evaluates true. `manual` = never recover automatically; alerts need manual handling, no recovery event is pushed, and `recovery` is not allowed.

recovery.description: Recovery evaluation config. Required (with non-empty `recovery.expr`) only when `recovery_mode` is `expression_match` or `recovery_query_match`; must be omitted for the other modes.

absent_counts_as_normal.description: Count an active instance that is missing from every condition query of a successful round as one normal round, instead of freezing the instance in its current state. Only valid with `recovery_mode` `condition_clear` or `expression_match`; omitting it keeps the freeze-on-absence behavior of existing rules. The matched datasources must be served by monit-edge v0.77.0 or later, otherwise saving the rule fails with `InvalidParameter`.

AlertRuleAnyDataV2.description: Any-data check configuration (lifecycle v2). Fires when a query returns any data row.

enabled.description: Whether the any-data check is enabled: any returned data row triggers an alert.

alerting_check_times.description: Fire after the alert condition is met this many times; when enabled, minimum 1 and maximum 10000. Combined with `alerting_window_size` it means at least N hits within the last M evaluations.

alerting_window_size.description: Optional sliding window size M: fire only when the condition is met at least `alerting_check_times` times within the last M evaluations. Omit for consecutive mode. Must satisfy `alerting_check_times` <= M <= 10000.

recovery_check_times.description: Recover after the recovery condition is met this many times; minimum 1 when enabled.

severity.description: Severity of any-data alerts, case-sensitive; required when enabled.

recovery_mode.description: How recovery is decided (lifecycle v2); required when enabled. `data_absent` = recover when the query returns no data; `recovery` is not allowed. `recovery_query_match` = recover when the `recovery.expr` query expression evaluates true; only a single query (`name=A`) is allowed. `manual` = never recover automatically; alerts need manual handling, no recovery event is pushed, and `recovery` is not allowed.

recovery.description: Recovery evaluation config. Required (with non-empty `recovery.expr`) only when `recovery_mode` is `recovery_query_match`; must be omitted for the other modes.

enabled.description: Whether the per-series no-data check is enabled: series that previously reported data trigger an alert when data disappears.

severity.description: Severity of no-data alerts, case-sensitive; required when the per-series check is enabled.

alert_on_empty_result.description: Whether to alert when all queries return empty results (global empty-result check).

alert_on_empty_result_severity.description: Severity of empty-result alerts, case-sensitive; only takes effect and is required when `alert_on_empty_result` is on.

alerting_check_times.description: Fire after the alert condition is met this many times; when enabled, minimum 1 and maximum 10000. Combined with `alerting_window_size` it means at least N hits within the last M evaluations.

alerting_window_size.description: Optional sliding window size M: fire only when the condition is met at least `alerting_check_times` times within the last M evaluations. Omit for consecutive mode. Must satisfy `alerting_check_times` <= M <= 10000.

recovery_check_times.description: Recover after the recovery condition is met this many times; minimum 1 when enabled.

end_mode.description: How a no-data alert ends (lifecycle v2); required when enabled. `data_reappears` = recover when data reappears. `data_reappears_or_timeout` = end when data reappears or after `auto_close_after_seconds` seconds, whichever comes first; requires the per-series no-data check and a positive `auto_close_after_seconds`. `manual` = never end automatically; alerts need manual handling and no recovery event is pushed. For `data_reappears` and `manual`, `auto_close_after_seconds` must be 0.

auto_close_after_seconds.description: Seconds to wait before auto-closing. Allowed and required to be positive only when `end_mode` is `data_reappears_or_timeout`; must be 0 for the other modes.

AlertRuleRecoveryQueryV2.description: Recovery evaluation configuration for lifecycle v2.

expr.description: Recovery condition expression: a threshold expression (e.g. `$A < 90`) in `expression_match` mode, a query expression in `recovery_query_match` mode. Required and non-empty when the corresponding mode is enabled.

value_fields.description: Numeric result fields the recovery expression references as `$A.<field>`; same semantics as a query's `value_fields`. Not returned when empty.

args.description: Datasource-specific parameters for the recovery query; keys follow the same `<datasource>.<param>` convention as a query's `args`. Not returned when empty.

InvestigationTarget.description: Alert-event drill-down entry. A deliberately closed tagged union: new kinds require explicit server support, and unknown fields inside a target are rejected.

kind.description: Entry kind: `dashboard` opens a dashboard panel, `query` opens an Explore query. It decides whether `dashboard` or `query` must be supplied; supplying the other one is rejected.

purpose.description: One-sentence plain text explaining what this entry helps confirm during investigation. Literal text, not a template, and not part of the alert identity. At most 512 bytes; control characters are rejected.

time_range.description: Window around the event time, required on every saved entry. A zero-length window is rejected; defaults belong to the editor.

query.description: Configuration for the `query` kind; required when `kind` is `query`, and rejected when `kind` is `dashboard`.

dashboard.description: Configuration for the `dashboard` kind; required when `kind` is `dashboard`.

DashboardInvestigationTarget.description: Configuration of a dashboard drill-down entry.

dashboard_id.description: Target dashboard ID; must be a canonical UUIDv7.

target_id.description: Panel ID inside the dashboard; must be a canonical UUIDv7. Optional.

variables.description: Dashboard variable values, keyed by variable name. Values may reference event labels through `{{ }}` templates; defaults to an empty object.

InvestigationTimeRange.description: Window around the alert event time, expressed as two offsets. Both directions must be non-negative and at least one must be greater than zero, so an entry never resolves to an empty window.

before_seconds.description: Seconds to look back from the event time.

after_seconds.description: Seconds to look forward from the event time, so behaviour after the event stays visible.

QueryInvestigationTarget.description: Explore query used by a `query` drill-down entry. The expression may reference event labels through `{{ }}` templates, while `args` values may not.

datasource_id.description: Data source the query runs against. Omit (or set 0) to run on the alert event's own datasource.

DashboardQuery.description: Query payload shared by dashboard panels and alert rule drill-down entries. Template syntax differs by context: dashboard panels use dashboard variables (`${name}`), drill-down entries use event labels (`{{ }}`).

mode.description: Evaluation mode: `instant` = evaluate at a single timestamp; `range` = evaluate a stepped series over the time range; `window` = return raw rows inside the time range. Dashboard panels on Prometheus and Loki accept `instant` or `range` (Loki `logs` panels need `range`); MySQL panels need `window`.

expr.description: Query expression in the datasource's language. In dashboard panels it may reference variables as `${name}`, `${name:raw}` (one value inserted as is) or `${name:regex}` (values joined as a regex alternation), or as `$name` in Prometheus and Loki; write `$${...}` for a literal. Without a formatter, multi-value or `all` variables and values inside `=~`/`!~` are inserted in regex form, so they cannot be used with `=` or `!=`. MySQL queries do not support variables. In drill-down entries the expression may reference event labels through `{{ }}` templates.

args.description: Named query arguments; defaults to an empty object. In dashboard panels values may use `${name}` templates except for Loki and MySQL datasources. In drill-down entries keys and values must not contain `{{ }}` templates.

min_step_seconds.description: Minimum step, in seconds; must be greater than zero. In drill-down entries it is only accepted when `mode` is `range`. Omit or pass null to let the server decide.

DashboardDefinition.description: Complete dashboard payload stored as a portable `dashboard.v1` document. Unknown keys, duplicate keys, trailing values and nesting deeper than 32 levels are rejected, and the serialized form must stay within 1 MiB. Limits: 10 tabs, 10 sections per tab, 30 panels and 100 queries per tab, 100 panels and 300 queries per dashboard, 20 variables.

title.description: Dashboard title, 1–189 Unicode code points after trimming.

description.description: Optional description, at most 1024 Unicode code points.

refresh_interval.description: Auto-refresh cadence applied by the console: `off` disables auto-refresh; `30s` = every 30 seconds; `1m` = every minute; `5m` = every 5 minutes.

variables.description: Dashboard variables, at most 20, with unique names. Variables may reference other variables but not in a cycle.

tabs.description: Tabs, 1–10. Every tab, section and panel `id` must be a canonical UUIDv7 used only once across the definition. Tab titles do not need to be unique.

DashboardRelativeTimeRange.description: Relative time window. `from` is one of the fixed presets the validator accepts; `to` is always the literal string `now`.

from.description: Start offset relative to `to`: `now-15m` = 15 minutes ago; `now-30m` = 30 minutes ago; `now-1h` = 1 hour ago; `now-3h` = 3 hours ago; `now-6h` = 6 hours ago; `now-12h` = 12 hours ago; `now-24h` = 24 hours ago; `now-7d` = 7 days ago.

to.description: End of the window; only `now` is accepted.

DashboardTab.description: A top-level tab. Panels can sit directly on the tab (`top_panels`) or inside sections.

id.description: Canonical UUIDv7 identifying the tab; unique across the definition.

title.description: Tab title, 1–189 Unicode code points after trimming.

top_panels.description: Panels placed directly on the tab. A tab holds at most 30 panels in total, counting top panels and section panels, and at most 100 queries.

sections.description: Sections on the tab, at most 10.

DashboardSection.description: A collapsible group of panels inside a tab.

id.description: Canonical UUIDv7 identifying the section; unique across the definition.

collapsed.description: Whether the section renders collapsed by default.

panels.description: Panels in the section; they count toward the tab's 30-panel limit.

DashboardPanel.description: A single visualization. `datasource_ref` is required for every kind except `text`, where it is forbidden. Panels must not overlap inside the same container; the 24-column grid is validated on save.

id.description: Canonical UUIDv7 identifying the panel; unique across the definition.

queries.description: Queries in the panel. `time_series` accepts 1–26, `text` accepts none, every other kind accepts exactly one.

DashboardGridPosition.description: 24-column grid placement. `x` and `y` are zero-based; `x + w` must not exceed 24.

DashboardDatasourceRef.description: Points a panel or query variable at a datasource — either a fixed ID or a datasource variable evaluated at render time.

kind.description: `fixed` uses `datasource_id`; `variable` resolves `name` against a datasource variable.

datasource_id.description: Datasource ID. Required when `kind` is `fixed`, forbidden when `kind` is `variable`.

name.description: Name of a `datasource` variable in the same definition. Required when `kind` is `variable`, forbidden when `kind` is `fixed`.

datasource_type.description: Datasource type identifier: lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. The set is open, so saving accepts any such value, but the dashboard runtime only runs `prometheus`, `mysql` and `loki` datasources; panels on other types fail when run. With `kind` = `variable` it must equal the referenced datasource variable's `datasource_type`.

DashboardPanelQuery.description: One query inside a panel. `ref_id` labels the series in the panel and must be unique within the panel.

ref_id.description: Single uppercase letter (A–Z) naming the query inside its panel.

legend_alias.description: Optional legend label, at most 1024 Unicode code points. The console replaces `{{label}}` with that series label's value (for example `{{env}} requests`); dashboard variables are not substituted here.

DashboardVariable.description: A dashboard variable. Pick the arm with `kind`.

DashboardDatasourceVariable.description: Datasource selector variable. Its candidates are the account's datasources of `datasource_type`.

kind.description: Variable kind discriminator; always `datasource`, selecting a datasource.

name.description: Variable name, unique within the definition. Queries reference it as `${name}` (or `$name` inside Prometheus and Loki expressions). Names starting with `__` are reserved for the built-in variables `__interval`, `__rate_interval`, `__range` and `__auto`.

label.description: Optional display label; falls back to `name`.

datasource_type.description: Type of datasource offered as candidates; candidates are the account's enabled datasources of this type. The set is open, so saving accepts any such value, but the dashboard runtime only runs `prometheus`, `mysql` and `loki` datasources; panels on other types fail when run.

name_patterns.description: Wildcard patterns narrowing the candidates; empty means every datasource of the type.

default_datasource_id.description: Default datasource ID. Without a usable default the runtime picks the first candidate by name, then ID.

DashboardCustomVariable.description: Variable whose candidates come from a fixed list supplied inline.

kind.description: Variable kind discriminator; always `custom`, with candidates from a fixed list supplied inline.

name.description: Variable name, unique within the definition. Queries reference it as `${name}` (or `$name` inside Prometheus and Loki expressions). Names starting with `__` are reserved for the built-in variables `__interval`, `__rate_interval`, `__range` and `__auto`.

label.description: Optional display label; falls back to `name`.

options.description: Candidate list, 1–1000 entries. Values must be non-empty, unique and must not be `$__all`.

DashboardQueryVariable.description: Variable whose candidates are resolved by running a query against a datasource.

kind.description: Variable kind discriminator; always `query`, with candidates resolved by running a query against a datasource.

name.description: Variable name, unique within the definition. Queries reference it as `${name}` (or `$name` inside Prometheus and Loki expressions). Names starting with `__` are reserved for the built-in variables `__interval`, `__rate_interval`, `__range` and `__auto`.

label.description: Optional display label; falls back to `name`.

refresh.description: When the candidates are recomputed: `on_dashboard_load` = once when the dashboard loads; `on_time_range_change` = every time the time range changes.

mode.description: Selection cardinality: `single` makes the resolved selection hold exactly one value; `multi` allows multiple values.

include_all.description: When true the variable also offers an `all` selection.

DashboardSelection.description: A concrete selection of variable values. As a saved variable `default`, `values` must be non-empty and hold exactly one value in `single` mode. In runtime requests an empty `values` array is valid and means unresolved — the server never substitutes a default for it.

kind.description: `values` selects the listed entries, `all` selects everything (only allowed when `include_all` is true).

values.description: Selected values, unique and never `$__all`. Must be empty when `kind` is `all`.

DashboardCandidate.description: One selectable option of a custom variable.

DashboardVariableQuery.description: Variable query. Pick the arm with `kind`; the arm must match the referenced datasource type.

kind.description: Query kind discriminator; always `prometheus`, a label-values query against Prometheus.

metric.description: Optional metric selector that restricts the series considered; may reference other variables as `${name}` or `$name`.

label_filters.description: Optional matchers narrowing the series before label values are read.

label.description: Prometheus label name to match, e.g. `job`; letters, digits, `_`, `:`, `.` and `-`, starting with a letter or `_`.

op.description: Matcher operator: `=` = equals; `!=` = not equals; `=~` = regex match; `!~` = regex does-not-match.

value.description: Matcher value; may reference other variables as `${name}`. A multi-value or `all` variable needs `=~` or `!~`.

DashboardSQLVariableQuery.description: SQL query returning one column of candidates.

kind.description: Query kind discriminator; always `sql`, a SQL query returning one column of candidates.

expr.description: SQL statement whose result supplies the candidates. SQL variable queries run only on MySQL datasources, and MySQL queries do not support variable references.

args.description: Named query arguments; defaults to an empty object.

text_field.description: Column used as the candidate label; defaults to the value column.

value_field.description: Column used as the candidate value.

DashboardLogsVariableQuery.description: Logs query returning one field's values as candidates.

kind.description: Query kind discriminator; always `logs`, a logs query returning one field's values as candidates.

expr.description: Logs query expression; may reference other variables as `${name}`. Logs variable queries run only on Loki datasources, where `expr` may be empty to list the field's values across all streams.

field.description: Log field whose values become candidates. For a Loki datasource it must be a bare stream label name (letters, digits and underscores).

target_id.description: Optional tab, section or panel ID to focus in the target dashboard.

variable_mappings.description: Values to set in the target dashboard, keyed by target variable name (must match `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}$`); each entry says where the value comes from. Send `{}` for none.

DashboardLinkMapping.description: One entry of a drill-down variable mapping.

source.description: Where the value comes from: `variable` = the current value of a variable of the source dashboard (requires `name`), allowed on table and bar panels; `row_column` = the clicked row's value in a table column (requires `column`), table panels only; `category` = the clicked bar's category, `series` = its series name, `value` = its value — these three are bar panels only and take no extra fields.

name.description: Variable of the source dashboard to read; required when `source` is `variable` and must exist in the same definition; forbidden for other sources.

DashboardAbsoluteTimeRange.description: Absolute evaluation window. Both bounds are Unix timestamps in milliseconds, `from_ms` must be less than `to_ms`, and neither may exceed the JavaScript safe integer limit.

from_ms.description: Start of the window as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Must be 0 or greater and less than `to_ms`.

to_ms.description: End of the window as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Must be greater than `from_ms`; `instant` queries are evaluated at this time.

DashboardRuntimeError.description: Failure of one variable or one query. A failed variable or query does not fail the whole call.

reason.description:
Machine-readable failure reason. The set is open; current values:
- `invalid_request`: the query or datasource setup is rejected (unsupported datasource type or query mode, non-empty `args` where none are allowed, a malformed argument).
- `variable_invalid`: a variable could not be used (no selection and no default, a selection outside the candidates, an unresolved dependency, a bad substitution, or an unusable candidate list).
- `panel_missing`: the panel is not in the dashboard (queries resolve only).
- `datasource_permission_denied`: the datasource is missing, disabled, not accessible to the caller, or no accessible datasource matches the variable.
- `field_missing`, `value_not_scalar`, `empty_field_name`, `duplicate_field_name`, `field_type_changed`: the result does not fit the panel's visualization, or a SQL variable query returned unusable columns.
- `timeout`: the datasource call timed out; `panel_deadline`: the run hit the overall 35-second deadline.
- `canceled`, `panel_canceled`: the call was cancelled.
- `overloaded`: the datasource side is rate limiting.
- `too_many_rows`, `result_too_large`, `source_too_large`: a row, size or candidate-count limit was exceeded.
- `edge_unavailable`, `no_active_edge`, `edge_upgrade_required`, `edge_version_unknown`, `mixed_edge_versions`: the Edge cluster of the datasource is not connected, too old, of unknown version, or mixed.
- `internal`: an unexpected server-side error.

message.description: Human-readable detail for display or troubleshooting; its wording is not stable, so do not parse it.

DashboardRuntimeDatasource.description: The datasource a runtime variable or query was bound to.

id.description: Datasource ID, as listed by the datasource list endpoint.

type.description: Datasource type identifier. Resolved queries and `query` variables only use `prometheus`, `mysql` or `loki`; the datasource chosen by a `datasource` variable can be any type identifier the variable was configured with.

name.description: Datasource name.

DashboardResolvedVariable.description: One resolved variable. A failure (no selection and no default, a selection outside the candidates, an unresolved dependency, an unreachable datasource, an unusable query result) fills `error` and leaves `selection` out instead of failing the request.

name.description: Variable name, as defined in the dashboard or draft.

kind.description: Variable kind: `datasource` = selects a datasource; `custom` = fixed inline list; `query` = resolved by running a query.

candidates.description: Selectable options, at most 1000; an empty array when there are none or resolution failed. Order: `custom` keeps the definition order, `datasource` is sorted by name then ID, `query` is sorted by value.

DashboardVariablesResolveRequest.description: Resolve every variable of a stored dashboard against a time range and the caller's current selections.

dashboard_id.description: Canonical UUIDv7 of the dashboard.

variables.description: Selections already made, keyed by variable name, at most 20 entries. Variables without an entry fall back to their stored defaults; a name the dashboard does not define fails the call with HTTP 400.

DashboardVariablesResolveResponse.description: Resolved variables plus the effective selection for each name.

dashboard_id.description: ID of the dashboard the variables were resolved for, echoing the request.

selections.description: Effective selections keyed by variable name; only variables that resolved successfully appear.

DashboardResolvedQuery.description: One query bound to a concrete datasource with its variables substituted.

ref_id.description: Query reference within the panel: a single letter `A`–`Z`.

mode.description: Evaluation mode: `range` = a stepped time series; `instant` = a single point in time; `window` = rows inside a bounded time window. Prometheus and Loki queries use `range` or `instant`; MySQL queries use `window`.

expr.description: Expression with variable templates substituted. Built-in time variables stay verbatim when the request set `preserve_builtin_variables` to `true`.

args.description: Query arguments; an empty object when none. Only Loki queries carry arguments: `loki.limit` (a decimal integer from 1 to 1000, the maximum number of log entries) and `loki.direction` (`latest` or `earliest`).

min_step_seconds.description: Minimum step in seconds from the panel query; omitted when unset.

DashboardResolvedPanelQueries.description: Per-panel resolution result. `state` is `success` when every query resolved, `partial` when some did and `error` when none did. `error` describes only the first failure.

panel_id.description: ID of the panel, echoing an entry of `panel_ids`.

state.description: Resolution state of the panel's queries: `success` = every query resolved; `partial` = some resolved and some failed; `error` = none resolved, including a panel that does not exist.

queries.description: Queries that resolved successfully, in the panel's query order. Queries that failed are left out; empty array when none resolved.

DashboardQueriesResolveRequest.description: Resolve the queries of selected panels without executing them, so a client can preview datasource binding and variable substitution.

dashboard_id.description: Canonical UUIDv7 of the dashboard.

panel_ids.description: Panels to resolve, 1–100 unique IDs. A panel that does not exist yields an `error` arm rather than failing the call.

variables.description: Selections keyed by variable name, at most 20 entries. Variables without an entry fall back to their stored defaults; a name the dashboard does not define fails the call with HTTP 400.

max_data_points.description: Target maximum number of points per series, used to compute the step and render the built-in time variables. 2–5000; omit or send null for the default of 100.

preserve_builtin_variables.description: Keep built-in time variables verbatim in the resolved expressions so a caller with its own execution window can render them; user variables are still resolved.

DashboardQueriesResolveResponse.description: Resolved queries of the requested panels, plus the effective variable selections they were resolved with. Nothing is executed.

dashboard_id.description: ID of the dashboard the queries were resolved against, echoing the request.

variables.description: Effective selections of the variables that resolved successfully, keyed by variable name; variables that failed to resolve are left out.

panels.description: One entry per requested panel, in request order.

DashboardPanelRunBudget.description: Execution accounting for a panel run.

max_concurrency.description: Maximum number of the panel's queries executed at the same time; fixed at 6.

execution_count.description: Number of queries that resolved successfully and were dispatched for execution; queries that failed to resolve are not counted.

DashboardPanelRunRef.description: Result of one query inside a panel run or preview. The raw execution payload differs per datasource type and is passed through unmodified, so it is not schema-constrained here.

ref_id.description: Query reference within the panel: a single letter `A`–`Z`, as set in the panel's `queries`.

state.description: Per-query state: `success` = the query ran and `execution` is present; `error` = the query could not be resolved or executed, or the run was cancelled or timed out, and `error` explains why; `incompatible` = the query ran, but its result does not fit the panel's visualization (for example a configured field is missing or not numeric), so `execution` is still present and `error` explains the mismatch.

child_request_id.description: Request ID of the underlying datasource execution; use it when tracing a single query. Absent when the query never reached the datasource.

execution.description: Datasource-specific execution result, passed through unmodified. Present when `state` is `success` or `incompatible`; absent when `state` is `error`.

DashboardPanelRunRequest.description: Execute one panel of a stored dashboard. Omit `revision` (or send 0) to run the current revision; send it to have a stale call rejected. Text panels cannot be run.

dashboard_id.description: Canonical UUIDv7 of the dashboard.

panel_id.description: ID of the panel to execute. It must belong to the dashboard, otherwise the call returns `TargetNotFound` (HTTP 404).

revision.description: Revision guard. When set (non-zero) it must equal the dashboard's current revision, otherwise the call fails with `DashboardRevisionConflict` (HTTP 409). Omit or send 0 to skip the check.

variables.description: Selections keyed by variable name, at most 20 entries. Variables without an entry fall back to their stored defaults; a name the dashboard does not define fails the call with HTTP 400.

max_data_points.description: Target maximum number of points per series for `range` queries; the server derives the query step from it. 2–5000; omit or send null for the default of 100.

DashboardPanelRunResponse.description: Panel execution result. HTTP 200 is returned even when every query failed; read `run_state` and each ref's `state` and `error`. A response larger than 8 MiB is rejected with `EntityTooLarge` (HTTP 413) instead of being truncated.

dashboard_id.description: ID of the dashboard that was run, echoing the request.

panel_id.description: ID of the panel that was run, echoing the request.

run_state.description: Aggregate state of the run: `success` = every query succeeded; `partial` = at least one query succeeded and at least one did not; `cancelled` = no query succeeded and the client cancelled the request; `incompatible` = no query succeeded and at least one query ran but returned a result that does not fit the panel's visualization; `error` = no query succeeded and none is `incompatible` (also when the panel has no queries).

variables.description: Effective selections of the variables that resolved successfully, keyed by variable name; variables that failed to resolve are left out.

refs.description: One entry per query of the panel, in the panel's query order. A query that failed to resolve appears with `state` `error`.

DashboardDraftContext.description: Where an unsaved draft panel or variable set belongs. `existing` targets a stored dashboard, `new` a folder that does not contain one yet — the two are mutually exclusive.

kind.description: Draft context kind: `existing` = targets a stored dashboard (`dashboard_id` required); `new` = a folder that does not contain one yet (`folder_id` required).

dashboard_id.description: Required for `existing`, forbidden for `new`. The caller must have access to the dashboard's folder.

folder_id.description: Required for `new`, forbidden for `existing`. Must be a folder the caller can access, otherwise the call returns `FolderNotFound` (HTTP 404).

DashboardVariablesPreviewRequest.description: Resolve a draft set of variables that is not stored in any dashboard yet.

variables.description: Draft variables, at most 20. They are validated like a stored definition (names, dependencies, option limits) and must stay within 1 MiB.

selections.description: Selections keyed by variable name, at most 20 entries. Variables without an entry fall back to their draft default; a name that is not in `variables` fails the call with HTTP 400.

DashboardVariablesPreviewResponse.description: Resolved draft variables. There is no `dashboard_id` because nothing is persisted.

variables.description: Resolved variables, in the order of the draft `variables`.

selections.description: Effective selections keyed by variable name; only variables that resolved successfully appear.

DashboardPanelPreviewRequest.description: Execute a draft panel inline, without saving a dashboard revision. The draft `panel` and `variables` together must stay within 1 MiB, and the request body within 2 MiB.

variables.description: Draft variables the panel may reference, at most 20. Required; the panel's queries can only use variables listed here.

selections.description: Selections keyed by variable name, at most 20 entries. Variables without an entry fall back to their draft default.

max_data_points.description: Target maximum number of points per series for `range` queries; the server derives the query step from it. 2–5000; omit or send null for the default of 100.

DashboardPanelPreviewResponse.description: Draft panel execution result. Same shape as a stored panel run, minus `dashboard_id` and `revision`. HTTP 200 is returned even when every query failed; a response larger than 8 MiB is rejected with `EntityTooLarge` (HTTP 413).

panel_id.description: ID of the draft panel, echoing `panel.id` from the request.

run_state.description: Aggregate state of the run: `success` = every query succeeded; `partial` = at least one query succeeded and at least one did not; `cancelled` = no query succeeded and the client cancelled the request; `incompatible` = no query succeeded and at least one query ran but returned a result that does not fit the panel's visualization; `error` = no query succeeded and none is `incompatible` (also when the panel has no queries).

variables.description: Effective selections of the variables that resolved successfully, keyed by variable name; variables that failed to resolve are left out.

refs.description: One entry per query of the panel, in the panel's query order. A query that failed to resolve appears with `state` `error`.

FolderItem.description: A monitor folder. Folders form a tree; `parent_path` is the comma-separated ancestor ID list, so the caller can rebuild the tree and search it client-side.

id.description: Folder ID. Pass it as `id` to update, move, or delete the folder, as `parent_id` or `dest_parent_id` to nest folders under it, and as `folder_id` on alert rules and dashboards.

parent_id.description: Parent folder ID; 0 at the root.

parent_path.description: Comma-separated ancestor IDs from the root, excluding this folder; empty at the root.

team_id.description: ID of the team the folder belongs to; 0 when it has no team. Members of the team can see and modify the folder.

name.description: Folder name.

creator_id.description: Member ID of the creator; the creator can always see and modify the folder.

updater_id.description: Member ID of the last updater. Updates and moves both set it.

created_at.description: Creation time as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

updated_at.description: Time of the last update or move as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

FolderCreateRequest.description: Request to create a monitor folder.

name.description: Folder name; required, and must not contain a period (`.`), slash (`/`), or comma (`,`).

parent_id.description: ID of the parent folder; 0 or omitted creates a root folder. The caller must be allowed to modify the parent.

team_id.description: ID of the team the folder belongs to; 0 or omitted means no team. Members of the team can see and modify the folder and everything below it.

FolderUpdateRequest.description: Request to update a monitor folder. Editable fields are replaced as a whole.

id.description: ID of the folder to update, from `/monit/folder/list` or the create response.

name.description: New folder name; required, and must not contain a period (`.`), slash (`/`), or comma (`,`).

note.description: New note. Omitted or empty clears the note.

team_id.description: New team ID; 0 or omitted removes the team assignment.

FolderMoveRequest.description: Request to move a monitor folder and its descendants.

id.description: ID of the folder to move, from `/monit/folder/list`.

dest_parent_id.description: ID of the new parent folder; send 0 to move to the root. The field cannot be omitted. Must differ from `id` and must not be a descendant of the folder.

FolderDeleteRequest.description: Request to delete a monitor folder.

id.description: ID of the folder to delete, from `/monit/folder/list`. The folder must be empty.

FolderHealthItem.description: Health summary for a visible folder.

folder_id.description: ID of the folder this entry describes; matches `id` in `/monit/folder/list`.

has_issue.description: `true` when a rule in this folder or in any descendant has an active alert or a runtime problem (`runtime_state` of `offline`, `abnormal`, `stale`, or `no_datasource`). Rules in folders the caller cannot read are not counted.

items.description: One health entry per folder visible to the caller, sorted by `folder_id`.
